minutes.headline: Water commissioners moved to approve the FY25 operating budget; a separate bill line for the main replacement bond is planned.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners finalized the FY2024-25 operating budget and a motion to approve was made, though the result is not in the captions. They reviewed warrant articles, dropping the leak detection article, discussed a bylaw conflict with Mass General Law, and planned a separate bill line for the Massachusetts Avenue water main replacement bond. Updates covered the Hickory Hills pilot study, public education, PFAS litigation and the main project.

votes.motion: Approve the maintenance and operation budget for 2024 (FY2425).

budget_items.what_was_said: Final health insurance numbers came in lower than expected; the budget carries a higher rate to be safe.
Dental is a small expense and was kept at the earlier figure.
A separate equipment replacement/services line was restored after being squeezed out in the past.
Utilities for all wells and the building were discussed; electric costs have risen and are expected to rise further with treatment plants.
Solar has no numbers yet; it would wait for next March's annual warrant rather than a special town meeting.
A quote for whole-town leak detection was obtained; it will come out of the regular maintenance budget rather than a warrant article.
Prices for replacement SUVs were being looked at.

budget_items.topic: Mass Ave water main replacement bond line item
budget_items.what_was_said: A new quarterly bill line item would collect the estimated bond cost over 20 years, based on the temporary borrowing, and be adjusted when the final bond is set.
Permit comments on the paving section could mean a change order on a bid already placed.

decisions.decision: Leak detection article (Article Six) to be removed from the warrant; cost to come from the operating budget.
Leave the bylaw conflict for now; the chair will reach out to the bylaw's submitters to invite them to a workshop to clean it up themselves.
Warrant articles go to counsel (KP) for review; commissioners to vote and sign at the next meeting for posting in early March.
Proceed with the bill insert in the April bills announcing the new line item, based on the temporary borrowing figure.

what_happened.line: A motion to approve the FY2425 maintenance and operation budget was made, but the result is not audible in the captions.
The leak detection article (Article Six) was removed from the warrant; its cost is to come from the operating budget instead.
Commissioners agreed to a new quarterly bill line for the Mass Ave water main replacement bond, with a bill insert in the April bills.
The bylaw conflict with Mass General Law was left for now; the chair will invite the submitters to a workshop to clean it up.
Warrant articles go to counsel for review, with a vote and signatures planned at the next meeting for posting in early March.

why_it_matters: Water district customers will see a new line on their quarterly bill for the Mass Ave main replacement bond, set from the temporary borrowing and adjusted when the final bond is set.
Moving leak detection from a warrant article into the operating budget means it is not put to a separate town meeting vote, and the cost is carried in the budget behind the rates.
